title: Release 0.5.0: parse with saphyr-parser instead of yaml-rust2
description:
Switches the parser backend from `yaml-rust2` 0.11 to `saphyr-parser` 0.1 and releases 0.5.0. The value type is unchanged. Research, decisions and the classified location diff are in `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-08-saphyr-migration.md`; strands `qy-fr4j7ft8` (this work) and `qy-block-scalar-utf8-drift-7dccrmto` (the bug).

## Why

yaml-rust2's scanner advances its marker by bytes instead of chars for the part of a block-scalar line past its lookahead buffer, so every span after a non-ASCII `|`/`>` scalar drifts and content provenance for later scalars comes back `None`. The bug is still in yaml-rust2 0.13.0, whose README now says the crate gets basic maintenance only. saphyr-parser, the same author's successor, counts chars. In the Quarto schema fixture `definitions.yml` this takes the number of scalars without content provenance from 3,687 to 0.

## What changes for consumers

- `YamlWithSourceInfo::yaml` is still yaml-rust2's `Yaml`, now also re-exported as `quarto_yaml::Yaml` and `quarto_yaml::yaml::{Array, Hash}`. Please name it through `quarto_yaml`: a later release replaces the re-export with a type defined here (`qy-0qodo40x`). yaml-rust2 stays as a dependency for that type only, without its `encoding` feature.
- A missing value (`key:` with nothing after it) is now a zero-width span just after the colon, so `entry_span` of `a:` is `"a:"`. Previously it sat on the next token (the next key, or the end of the input). An empty key stays on its colon; a missing block-sequence item sits at the end of its `- ` line.
- An empty block scalar followed by a key no longer spans the next entry (`qy-ky0yjkim`).
- Flow-pair mappings inside flow sequences (`[ {a: b}:c ]`) no longer extend to the closing `]`.
- "did not find expected key" on bad indentation points at the under-indented key rather than at its colon.
- yaml-test-suite cases 4H7K (extra `]`) and BS4K (comment intercepting a multi-line plain scalar) are now rejected, as the suite requires. No input that was accepted and is spec-valid changed status; disagreements with the suite went from 9 to 7.

Everything else (block-scalar span rule, tag spans, quoted and plain spans, error messages) is unchanged. `Marker::index` still counts chars in saphyr, so the char-to-byte cursor stays.

## How the diff was verified

The first commit adds `crates/quarto-yaml/tests/golden.rs`: insta snapshots of every node's span, value, content provenance and tag for 60 hand-written edge cases, the 402 yaml-test-suite inputs, and the schema fixtures, captured with the yaml-rust2 backend. The second commit's snapshot diff is every location change the swap makes; each is in one of the categories above.

Under `strict-provenance` the golden tests are ignored: the corpus contains 15 inputs the provenance walk could not derive before this change either (`qy-0ongzhi7`).

## q2

q2's six dependent crates (`8ae461f1b`) were tested against this branch via a temporary `[patch.crates-io]` and compared with an unpatched run on the same machine: 11,717 passed / 145 failed with the branch vs 11,731 / 131 unpatched, across 19 test binaries. The failure sets overlap almost entirely (pandoc "current working directory no longer exists", typst, julia, engine fixtures); the 16 tests failing only with the branch all pass when re-run against it single-threaded, so nothing is attributable to the swap.

title: Release 0.4.0: locate YAML syntax errors in the source
description:
Fixes strand `qy-scan-error-location-f9r4yvxq` (consumed by q2 `bd-x30aq7ae`). Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-08-scan-error-location.md`.

## Problem
Every YAML syntax error came back as `Error::ParseError { location: None, .. }`. The only position was yaml-rust2's `"… at byte N line L column C"` suffix in the message. `N` counts chars, not bytes, and `L`/`C` are relative to the parsed string, so with `parse_with_parent` (frontmatter, cell options) they don't match lines in the actual file.

## Change
- `parse_impl` builds the error in `YamlBuilder::scan_error`, which converts the marker char→byte with `byte_offset_of_char` and maps it through the parent with `make_source_info_at_offset`, the same path node spans use. The span is the offending character, or zero-width when the marker sits at EOF.
- `message` is now the scanner's `info()` only.
- "No YAML document found" gets a zero-width location at the start of the content.
- `Display` is unchanged (`Parse error: {message}`). The TODO no-ops are gone, and the docs now point to quarto-error-reporting for rendering locations.
- Workspace version bumped to **0.4.0**. **Merging this PR publishes it.**

## Breaking: `From<yaml_rust2::ScanError> for Error` removed
This only affects code that calls yaml-rust2 0.11 directly and uses `?` to turn a `ScanError` into `quarto_yaml::Error`. To get the old behaviour exactly:
```rust
.map_err(|e| quarto_yaml::Error::ParseError { message: e.to_string(), location: None })
```
`parse` / `parse_file` / `parse_with_parent` callers are unaffected at compile time, but `location` is now populated and `message` no longer has the position suffix.

## Tests
`crates/quarto-yaml/tests/scan_errors.rs` (all 6 fail on `main`): file-offset mapping under a parent, a non-ASCII prefix (char vs byte), EOF clamping, `parse_file`'s FileId, the no-parent `FileId(0)` case, and the empty document. Locally: `cargo test --workspace`, clippy, and fmt are clean.

title: Release 0.1.3: scalar content provenance
description:
Add content provenance for decoded scalars.

`quarto-yaml` has always paired each scalar with a `SourceInfo` describing
its raw source text; consumers adding offsets into the *decoded* string to
that span drift — by one byte for a quoted scalar, by the stripped
indentation per line for a block scalar, by a collapsed fold per line
break. This release adds the missing piece: a second `SourceInfo`
describing the decoded content, derived by walking yaml-rust2's own
decoded value against the raw source in lockstep.

This is a patch release under the additive design: no public signature
changes, so every existing caller compiles untouched
(quarto-yaml-validation's 22 test sites, q2's 15, and this crate's own 5).
q2 needs no manifest edit — its `^0.1.2` pin already accepts 0.1.3.

What is new, for a consumer:

- `content_source_info() -> Option<&SourceInfo>` on `YamlWithSourceInfo`:
  the provenance of a scalar's decoded content, as opposed to
  `source_info`, which describes the node's source text — quotes
  included, and the per-line indentation that decoding strips. Adding a
  content offset to `source_info` would be wrong; this is the value to
  add content offsets to. "Content" means the decoded scalar text before
  type resolution — yaml-rust2's `Event::Scalar` value string — so `k: ~`
  has one content byte and `k: true` has four.
- `with_content_provenance()` for attaching it (the parser does this; it
  mirrors the existing `with_tag` idiom).
- The contract: if `Some(si)`, then `si.map_offset(k)` resolves content
  byte `k` to its true source position, and `si.length() == <decoded
  content>.len()`. An offset inside a collapsed break region resolves to
  the start of that region; every non-whitespace content byte is exact.
  That precision limit is a real trade, not a footnote.
- `None` has three causes, all meaning the same thing to a consumer
  (decline sub-offset arithmetic): not a scalar; no derivation ran
  (hand-built node, or an unresolved alias); or the derivation desynced,
  which is a bug in this crate. An empty scalar is not `None` — it derives
  to a zero-length `SourceInfo`.
- A new default-off `strict-provenance` feature: turns a desync into a
  panic naming both cursor offsets, and asserts that any scalar whose
  derivation ran is `Some`. CI now runs the suite with it on. It already
  earned its keep — it found a real desync (a plain scalar with a
  trailing space before a folded break) on its first run, a shape none of
  the 32 measured fixtures had covered.
- The `value_span` / `key_span` doc comments are corrected: they cover the
  source text including delimiters, not "just the value". That misreading
  is what caused the bug class this release fixes.

The derivation is verified against 43 measured fixtures produced by a
lockstep prototype run against yaml-rust2's own decoded output, not
against a proof.

Requires `quarto-source-map` >=0.1.3 for `ProvenanceBuilder`.

title: Capture YAML tags on sequences and mappings
description:
Fixes #14.

`quarto_yaml::parse*` only attached YAML tags to scalar nodes; tags arriving on `SequenceStart` / `MappingStart` events were silently discarded. Downstream, this made `!prefer` / `!concat` on arrays and maps a silent no-op in Quarto 2's config merge.

## Approach

Verified marker positions empirically against yaml-rust2 0.11 for every tagged-collection shape (see `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-08-collection-tags.md` for the full probe table):

- Flow collections and block sequences: the Start marker points at the collection's first token (`[`, `{`, or first `-`), so the existing backward tag-token walk works from there.
- **Block mappings**: the Start marker points at the *colon after the first key*, so walking back from it finds the key, not the tag. The walk must instead start from the first key's offset — which is exactly the offset `MappingEnd` already computes for the node span.

So: the raw tag is stashed on the `BuildNode` frame at the Start event, and located/attached at the End event, walking backward from the node's span start. `find_tag_span` now takes a byte offset instead of a `Marker` (scalar behavior unchanged), and the shared `make_tag_info` helper carries the same clamped in-bounds fallback the scalar path had.

`YamlWithSourceInfo::with_tag` (consuming builder, works for any node shape) is the new public surface; `new_scalar_with_tag` is untouched.

## Non-goals

- Standard tags (`!!seq`, `!!map`) are recorded like any other tag but not validated against the node shape, mirroring how application tags on scalars leave resolution alone.
- Node spans continue to exclude the tag (the tag has its own span), consistent with scalars.
- A comment between the tag and the collection (`k: !prefer # note`) defeats the walk-back and yields the fallback span — same pre-existing limitation as scalars; tracked as strand `qy-yqstv88w`, covered by an in-bounds test.

## Testing

14 new tests covering: block/flow sequences and mappings (incl. the block-mapping colon case), root-level tagged collections, anchor+tag in both orders, nested tagged collections, empty flow collections, standard tags, blank-line separation, multibyte offsets, comment fallback, and untagged collections staying `tag: None`. Also extends the spans-stay-in-bounds corpus. 363 workspace tests pass; clippy clean.

Braid strand: `qy-8pf7s9ot`. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-08-collection-tags.md`.

title: Include the closing bracket in flow-collection spans
description:
Fixes #10.

`yaml-rust2` reports `SequenceEnd` and `MappingEnd` at the closing `]` or `}`, so flow-collection spans ended one byte too early. This advances the end offset when the marker points at the expected closer. 

Flow mappings also use the stored `{` offset, while block mappings keep their existing first-key start.

title: Build spans from byte offsets, not yaml-rust2's char indices
description:
Fixes #9.

`SourceInfo` spans are documented and consumed as byte offsets, but were built from `yaml_rust2::Marker::index()`, which counts **characters** — the getter's doc says bytes, but the scanner increments it once per popped `char` ([scanner.rs#L46-L53](https://github.com/Ethiraric/yaml-rust2/blob/v0.11.0/src/scanner.rs#L46-L53) vs [#L60-L64](https://github.com/Ethiraric/yaml-rust2/blob/v0.11.0/src/scanner.rs#L60-L64)). One multi-byte character therefore shifted every later span, and made the units internally inconsistent: scalar lengths were measured in bytes while collection lengths were differences of character indices.

## Approach

Convert once, at the parser boundary, as the issue suggested:

- `YamlBuilder::new` precomputes a char-index → byte-offset table. For pure-ASCII sources (the common case) no table is built and the mapping is the identity, so there is no cost.
- A single conversion point, `byte_offset()`, replaces every raw `marker.index()` use — `make_source_info`, `compute_scalar_len`, `find_tag_span`, the tag-span fallback, and the three collection-length subtractions, so both span endpoints and all lengths are bytes.

With the issue's reprex, the second entry's span now resolves to exactly `"quoted"` (with its quotes). The correct range is `18..26` rather than the issue's predicted `20..28` — `é` is 2 bytes, so the value starts at byte 18.

## Tests

Three new regression tests cover scalar/key spans, collection and nested spans, and tag spans after multi-byte characters, and the spans-stay-within-the-source test gains multi-byte inputs.

Found along the way, filed separately as #10: flow-collection spans exclude the closing `]`/`}` (the `SequenceEnd`/`MappingEnd` marker points *at* the bracket). That predates this change and reproduces on pure-ASCII input, so it is left alone here, with a test comment marking it.

title: Switch the YAML backend from yaml-rust2 to saphyr
description:
@cscheid this is purely speculative but I thought it might be interested to know what would need to change.

---

Switches the YAML backend from `yaml-rust2` 0.11 to its maintained successor, `saphyr` / `saphyr-parser` 0.0.11.

The parser now implements saphyr's `SpannedEventReceiver`, which supplies both start and end markers per event. Plain- and block-scalar extents and flow-collection closers now come from the parser's own spans, replacing most of the hand-rolled span reconstruction (`plain_scalar_len`, `block_scalar_len`, and the flow-closer extension are gone). Two saphyr quirks keep some machinery: markers are still char-indexed, so the char→byte conversion from #11 stays; and quoted-scalar/flow-end span *ends* overshoot past trailing spaces and comments, so quoted scalars keep the escape-aware walker and collections read the end event's span start (which sits on the `]`/`}`) with the closer check from #12. Scalar resolution is unchanged — still our YAML 1.2 core-schema implementation, with the same hex/octal/overflow/tag behavior and tests.

**Stacked on #11 and #12**; their commits appear here until they merge.

## Changes required in downstream dependents

- **Dependency**: drop `yaml-rust2`; the value type is re-exported as `quarto_yaml::YamlOwned` / `quarto_yaml::ScalarOwned` (or depend on `saphyr` directly — `YamlWithSourceInfo::yaml` is now `saphyr::YamlOwned`).
- **Imports**: `use yaml_rust2::Yaml` → `use quarto_yaml::{ScalarOwned, YamlOwned}`; `yaml_rust2::yaml::Hash` → `saphyr::MappingOwned` (same `hashlink::LinkedHashMap` underneath, so `.insert()`/iteration code is unchanged).
- **Scalar variants** are now nested under `Value(…)`:
  - `Yaml::String(s)` → `YamlOwned::Value(ScalarOwned::String(s))`, and likewise `Integer`, `Boolean`, `Null`.
  - `Yaml::BadValue` → `YamlOwned::BadValue` and `Yaml::Alias(id)` → `YamlOwned::Alias(id)` (unchanged shape at the top level).
- **Collections renamed**: `Yaml::Array(vec)` → `YamlOwned::Sequence(vec)`; `Yaml::Hash(map)` → `YamlOwned::Mapping(map)`.
- **Floats are stored parsed**: `Yaml::Real(String)` → `YamlOwned::Value(ScalarOwned::FloatingPoint(OrderedFloat<f64>))`. Construct with `(1.5).into()`; read with `**f` or `as_floating_point()`. Any `.parse::<f64>()` on the old string payload should be deleted — an unparseable float can no longer exist. The source spelling (e.g. `1e3`) is no longer in the value; recover it via the node's span if needed.
- **Accessor renames** (on the YAML value; `YamlWithSourceInfo`'s own API — `as_hash()`, `get_hash_value()`, etc. — is unchanged): `as_i64()` → `as_integer()`, `as_f64()` → `as_floating_point()`. `as_str()`, `as_bool()`, and `as_vec()` keep their names; `as_hash()` on a raw value is now `as_mapping()`.
- **Exhaustive matches** on the value enum need two new arms: `YamlOwned::Representation(..)` and `YamlOwned::Tagged(..)`. quarto-yaml's parser never produces them (scalars are resolved eagerly; tags are reported out-of-band in `YamlWithSourceInfo::tag`), so a defensive arm is fine.

Plan and empirical findings: `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-01-switch-to-saphyr.md`.

title: Resolve scalars per the YAML 1.2 spec, and measure their spans against the source
description:
Fixes #2.

`YamlBuilder::on_event` typed every scalar from its text alone, discarding both the quote style and any explicit tag. 

## Scalar resolution

`parse_scalar_value` is replaced by `resolve_scalar`, which resolves in the order the spec requires:

1. **An explicit standard tag** (`!!int`, `!!str`, …) — A value that contradicts its tag (`!!int abc`) becomes `Yaml::BadValue`, as in yaml-rust2's loader. Verbatim spellings (`!<tag:yaml.org,2002:int>`) are handled too.
2. **The style** — any non-plain scalar, quoted or block, is a string.
3. **The core schema** on the plain text, unchanged apart from booleans (see below).

Application-specific tags (`!expr`, `!path`, …) still leave resolution alone and are reported in `YamlWithSourceInfo::tag` as before.

One deliberate deviation from yaml-rust2's loader: it checks the style *before* the tag, so `!!int "7"` comes out a string. An explicit tag is the node's type regardless of how the value is written, so we check the tag first and `!!int "7"` comes out as an `Integer(7)`.

## Booleans now follow 1.2, not 1.1

The core schema recognises only `true` / `false` (plus the `True`, `TRUE` spellings). `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off` and their case variants are now plain strings. 

## Spans

`compute_scalar_len` returned `value.len()` with a TODO about quotes and escapes. We now do it correctly, based on the style:

- **quoted** — scan to the matching close quote, handling `\` escapes and `''` doubling. The span covers the whole scalar, quotes included. 
- **plain** — walk the folded value back onto the source, so a multi-line plain scalar covers every line it occupies. Falls back to `value.len()` if value and source ever fail to line up, rather than guessing.
- **block** — scan content lines while blank or indented at least as far as the marker, leaving trailing blank lines out.

This shows up in `quarto-yaml-validation`'s diagnostic snapshot: the underline for `age: "not a number"` now covers the whole quoted string instead of stopping a byte short.

```
 1 │ age: "not a number"
   │      ───────┬──────
   │             ╰──────── Expected number, got string
```

## Two adjacent fixes in the same code path

- **Tag spans.** `find_tag_start_offset` reconstructed the tag's source text as  `!` + suffix and searched backwards for it, which gave the wrong span whenever the source spelling differed: `!!str` was reported as `!str` (off by one), and a `%TAG`-declared `!e!foo` as `!foo`.  `find_tag_span` now walks back over the node's properties. That also covers a tag separated from its value by an anchor (`key: !expr &name value`), where the old search found nothing and fell back to  a guessed span that could run *past the end of the source*. For example, for `key: !!str &name 5` it reported bytes 16..21 of an 18-byte document, panicking any consumer that sliced with it. The fallback is now clamped as well. All of this matters more since standard tags started carrying meaning.
- **A moot TODO.** `make_source_info` computed `column: start_column + len` under a `TODO: Calculate accurate end row/column`. `SourceInfo` is offset-only: `from_range` discards row and column, and consumers derive positions from offsets. Both helpers now call `SourceInfo::original` directly, like `make_tag_source_info` already did, and the dead plumbing is gone.

## Not in scope

Plain `0x1f` / `0o17` still resolve to strings rather than integers, diverging from the core schema and from yaml-rust2's own `from_str`. I filed that as #3.

title: Add CI release workflow (crates.io Trusted Publishing)
description:
Reference implementation for CI-driven releases across the quarto-* repos (plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-07-29-ci-releases-across-quarto-repos.md`, braid `qy-j7jz8rxi`/`qy-kkm4fm5o`).

**Release process after this merges:** open a PR bumping `[workspace.package] version` (and the intra-workspace `quarto-yaml` dep version), merge it — CI tests at the release commit, publishes both crates in dependency order, tags `vX.Y.Z`, and creates a GitHub Release with generated notes.

Design points:

- **Trusted Publishing (OIDC)** via `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@v1` — no stored tokens. Requires the one-time per-crate config on crates.io (owner `posit-dev`, repo `quarto-yaml`, workflow `release.yml`, environment `release`). Until that's configured, a release run would fail at the auth step and can simply be re-run after configuring.
- **Repo-agnostic:** publishable crates, dependency order, and the lockstep version are all derived from `cargo metadata`, so this exact file replicates to `quarto-source-map` and `quarto-error-reporting`. The check job fails loudly if workspace crates ever disagree on version.
- **Idempotent:** already-published crates are skipped, and tagging is a no-op when the tag exists, so a partially-failed release is fixed by re-running the workflow.
- **`cargo package --workspace` pre-flight** before any upload, so a packaging problem in the second crate can't strand a half-published release.
- **Dry-run mode:** `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run` runs check/test/package but skips auth, publish, and tagging — I'll use it to validate after merge.

The `release` GitHub environment already exists (created via API, no protection rules — the bump-PR merge is the human gate, per plan).

Verified locally: actionlint clean; the embedded planner script tested against all three repos (plans "nothing" at current versions) and against a synthetic unpublished 0.9.9 bump (plans both crates, correct order).

title: Resolve core-schema hex and octal integers
description:
Fixes #3.

Both `resolve_plain_scalar` and `resolve_tagged_scalar` parsed integers with the decimal-only `i64::from_str`, so the YAML 1.2 core schema's prefixed integer forms went astray: plain `0x1f` resolved to `String("0x1f")` and explicit `!!int 0x1f` to `BadValue`.

Both paths now go through a shared `parse_core_schema_int` helper implementing the three [core-schema](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#103-core-schema) `!!int` forms: `[-+]?[0-9]+`, `0o[0-7]+`, `0x[0-9a-fA-F]+`.

Details worth reviewing:

- **Digit runs are validated by hand** rather than left to `i64::from_str_radix`, which accepts a leading sign the schema doesn't — `0o+7` must stay a string.
- **The narrow cases stay strings**, per the issue's "should stay that way" table: `0X1f` (upper-case prefix), `-0x1f` / `+0x1f` (signed), `0b101` (no binary form), plus empty digit runs (`0x`), bad digits (`0o8`), and values overflowing `i64`.
- **Deliberate divergence from yaml-rust2 on the tagged path**: yaml-rust2's loader is also decimal-only for explicit `!!int` tags, so it gives `BadValue` for `!!int 0x1f`.
